title: Finite Gibbs-isometric Duhamel remainder
question: Can the all-time orbit-bound hypothesis in the finite-member Duhamel bridge be removed for each fixed finite Gibbs Hamiltonian, while keeping volume-uniformity and OS identification explicitly open?
method: For a finite self-adjoint H use the Gibbs functional calculus to obtain exact two-sided seminorm isometry of alpha_t.

Apply the finite-dimensional Taylor integral identity to R_t(X)=alpha_t(X)-X-t delta_H(X), then use Gibbs isometry under the integral to derive the t^2/2 bound from the single finite double commutator seminorm.
Check the two-level fixture independently and in Lean R248, and preserve the volume, source, cutoff, orientation, OS, KMS, gap and continuum firewalls.
finding: For every fixed finite Gibbs member, N_beta(R_t(X)) <= t^2 N_beta(delta_H^2(X))/2. The prior all-time orbit-envelope assumption is therefore unnecessary at fixed finite volume. The double-commutator constant may grow with volume, source or cutoff, and no common OS embedding is supplied.
decision_reason: This is the direct finite-member continuation after EXP-001065 and EXP-001062: it closes the exact Taylor/Duhamel remainder at finite dimension without pretending that finite-dimensional boundedness is a thermodynamic estimate.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite interface theorem. It does not prove actual Q3 four-context history, uniform direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, KMS/OS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or the TECT production owner.
